Description: applications.gymkhana.urls imports the new API layer, which fails because selectors/services import a non-existent Budget model. This blocks Django routing before legacy gymkhana handlers can run.
Suggested Fix: Remove the broken Budget import path or restore the intended model name consistently across selectors/services/API modules before routing the legacy module through the API layer.

Description: Documented voting handlers voting_poll, vote, and delete_poll are missing/commented out in applications.gymkhana.views, so the voting use cases and workflows have no executable backend implementation.
Suggested Fix: Restore and test the voting backend handlers or remove the dead routes and requirements traceability until implementation is completed.

Related Artifact: BR011 One Vote Per Student Per Poll
Description: Voting_voters has no unique_together or explicit uniqueness constraint, so one-vote-per-student is not enforced at the model layer.
Suggested Fix: Add a uniqueness constraint on (poll_event, student_id) and validate duplicate votes in the vote handler.

Description: Club_member defines no uniqueness constraint for (member, club), so duplicate same-club applications are not prevented by backend data constraints.
Suggested Fix: Add a unique constraint for the member/club pair and align the club_membership() error handling with that constraint.

Description: Club_budget.budget_amt uses the default IntegerField validator range and does not enforce a minimum of 0, allowing negative values.
Suggested Fix: Add MinValueValidator(0) or equivalent serializer/form validation for budget amounts.

Description: Club_member.status includes extra values beyond the documented enumeration open/confirmed/rejected, so the backend no longer matches the requirement definition.
Suggested Fix: Either tighten the documented rule to match the implementation or reduce the field choices to the required three-value enumeration.

Description: The requirement notes UI-only enforcement for minimum poll choices, which means the backend itself does not reject underspecified polls.
Suggested Fix: Enforce the minimum choice count in backend validation before poll creation.
